risk_notes: Flask dependency referenced via import but no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, or pinned version provided — unpinned third-party dependency.
Hardcoded fallback secrets in source: app.secret_key defaults to 'super-secret-flask-key' and LOCAL_ADMIN_TOKEN defaults to 'super-secret-admin-token' if env vars are unset.
Hardcoded default admin credentials: admin@example.com / adminpassword auto-created when the fallback admin bearer token is presented.
Password hashing uses unsalted SHA256 (services.py) instead of bcrypt/argon2 — explicitly declared as a non-goal but is a credential-storage risk.
Flask app runs with debug=True in __main__ — enables Werkzeug debugger/PIN, unsafe for any non-local deployment.
DATABASE_PATH defaults to 'database.db' in the working directory with no access controls noted.
Authentication fallback trusts unauthenticated X-User-Id and X-User-Email request headers to identify the current user (get_current_user), allowing trivial impersonation if the endpoint is reachable.
No dependency manifest (requirements.txt / Pipfile / pyproject.toml) present in the output — supply chain is fully unpinned and unauditable.
